To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The Swedish transportation sector can reduce its emissions of air pollutants by using existing technologies and by replacing fossil fuels in internal combustion engines with fuels from renewable sources.

(1) the average cost of reducing emissions of carbon dioxide by replacing fossil fuels by biomass-based fuels is estimated to $260/tonne CO2, at current fuel costs, (2) the cost of reducing emissions from the road transportation sector is much lower than that of reducing emissions from other sectors of the economy, such as the power generation sector, and (3) the cost of replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy sources is likely to decrease with further technical development and increased market penetration.
the use of fuels with low emissions of CO2, NOx, and other air pollutants can reduce emissions of these substances substantially.
In summary, our research is concerned with
strategies for reducing emissions from road transport in Sweden, and with the costs of these reductions.
the potential of reducing emissions of air pollution from transportation in a cost-effective and technically realistic way.
the development of a method for evaluating the environmental consequences of different strategies for the reduction of air pollutant emissions from the Swedish transportation system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Swedish transport sector is not expected to contribute significantly to the reduction of global warming, but that it can be made much less polluting in terms of local emissions of nitrogen oxide, sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide.
the Swedish transportation sector is well prepared to reduce emissions of air pollutants in the future, if the necessary political decisions are made and implemented.
it is possible to reduce the emissions from the Swedish transportation system by 80% by 2010 compared to 1990, with the use of today's best available technologies, at a cost of $1993 100-200/tonne C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of technical measures for reducing emissions of NOx and CO2 from the transportation sector, and measures for improving energy efficiency in the sector, can reduce emissions of both air pollutants and CO2, and can reduce fuel consumption, without increasing the costs of transportation.
a combination of measures is needed to reduce air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
it is possible to achieve substantial reductions in emissions of NOx, SO2, CO and hydrocarbons in the Swedish transportation sector by using existing technology and fuels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Swedish transportation sector can be made to contribute substantially to the reduction of emissions of air pollutants, and that this can be achieved at a cost which is not very different from the current cost of using fossil fuels.
there are many options available for reducing emissions of NOx and CO2 from the transportation sector in the near term.
the Swedish transportation sector has great potential to reduce its emissions of air pollutants.
